QF.id: Issue Management - General Obligations and Due Diligence_66

question.text: Equity shares held by a venture capital fund, Category I or Category II Alternative Investment Fund, or foreign venture capital investor in an IPO-bound company are subject to lock-in from which date?

answer.text: Date of allotment in the IPO
Date of listing of the company
Date of purchase by the VCF / Category I or II AIF / FVCI
Date of filing the offer document with SEBI

explanation.text: The Logic: For equity shares held by a venture capital fund, a Category I or Category II Alternative Investment Fund, or a foreign venture capital investor in an IPO-bound company, the lock-in start point is the date of purchase of those shares — not the date of allotment in the IPO or the date of listing. The Trap: "Date of allotment in the IPO" is the most common distractor because it is the reference point used for other shareholder categories. Candidates often assume the lock-in clock resets at the IPO for everyone. Note: The eligibility is limited to VCFs, Category I or Category II AIFs, and FVCIs; AIF in general (for example, Category III) is not covered by this date-of-purchase rule.
